meta.name: Fino corrections
meta.purpose: Corrections recorded since 5 November 2026, so a reader can see what changed and why. The list says nothing about errors that have not been found or recorded. The Fino connector's corrections() tool returns this list unchanged.
meta.status: 975 corrections are recorded. The list shows only the errors Fino found or was told about, so a page that is not on it is not proven correct: write to hello@finoprivacy.com and quote the decision number.

fields.fino_id: Decision number the correction concerns (YEAR/CC/NNN), or null if it concerns another page
fields.page_url: Public address of the corrected page
fields.what_was_wrong: The wrong statement, as it stood
fields.evidence_url: Where the right fact comes from (the regulator's original or an official text)
fields.reported_by: 'reader' or 'Fino check'. Readers are named only if they agree
fields.credit: Name of the reader, only with their agreement, otherwise null

corrections.what_it_says_now: The page shows EUR 900,000 as the fine that stands, "Reduced on appeal", and says what happened: the regulator announced EUR 10.4 million on 8 January 2021; the Landgericht Hannover set EUR 700,000 on 6 May 2024; the Oberlandesgericht Celle set EUR 900,000 on 18 December 2025 (3 ORbs 113/25), and the regulator's 2025 annual report says that decision is final (rechtskräftig). corrections.what_was_wrong: 15 Swedish decisions linked to the regulator's old host, datainspektionen.se, which no longer answers.

corrections.what_was_wrong: 108 decisions linked, as "the regulator's decision", to news reports, law firm articles, a post on X, a video, a file on Google Drive, a freedom-of-information portal, copies on GDPRhub or Datenschutzarchiv, court judgments, regulator news items and similar pages (and two to a home page).
